name: Black Basta Ransomware
desc: Black Basta is a RaaS (Ransomware as a Service), written in C++, that has been in development since February 2022 and in active use since April 2022. Operators using Black Basta employ a double-extortion technique where they encrypt files on the target systems and demand payment for the decryption key while also threatening to leak the information if they are not paid.

acts.d: Victims receive spear phishing emails with malicious zip files attached.
Due to password protection, the zip files are able to bypass some AV detections.
The zip files are extracted and usually contain a malicious document, such as a .doc, .pdf, or .xls.

acts.n: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
acts.d: The extracted files contain malicious macros.
Within the malicious files, encoded PowerShell scripts are used to download additional malicious scripts.

acts.n: Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Search Order Hijacking
acts.d: Black Basta uses Qakbot DLL files, which can exploit the Windows 7 calculator to execute malicious payloads.
regsvr32.exe is used to execute a malicious DLL
Accounts are created with names such as temp, r, or admin.

acts.n: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
acts.d: Benign-looking services are created for the ransomware binary.

acts.n: Domain Policy Modification: Group Policy Modification
acts.d: The Group Policy is modified for privilege escalation and defense evasion.
Qakbot is used for command-and-control communications
The new accounts are added to the administrator's group to maintain elevated access.
Cobalt Strike is deployed on the targeted system.
Modifications are made to the Registry.

acts.n: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify System Firewall
acts.d: Batch scripts, such as rdp.bat or SERVI.bat, are used to modify the firewall to allow remote administration and RDP.
Mimkatz is used to dump passwords.
Commands are used to discover domain account information.
Attackers discovered internal IP addresses typically found on the domain controller.
GetComputerName is used to query to the computer name
Legitimate tools, such as TeamViewer and AnyConnect, are installed and used on targeted systems.
RDP used for lateral movement.
Black Basta installs and uses PsExec to execute payloads on remote hosts.

acts.n: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
acts.d: BlackBasta disables Windows Defender with batch scripts, such as d.bat or defof.bat.
IsDebuggerPresent is used to check if processes are being debugged.
sc stop and taskkill is used to stop services.
The ransomware includes anti-analysis techniques that attempt to detect code emulation or sandboxing to avoid virtual/analysis machine environments.

acts.n: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
acts.d: BlackBasta collects data from infected systems.
Cobalt Strike is used for command-and-control communications.
BlackBasta exfiltrates data from the network prior to encrypting files.
Invoke-TotalExec is used to push out the ransomware binary.
BlackBasta deletes volume shadow copies using vssadmin.

BlackBasta leverages double extortion as part of its attacks. The group not only executes ransomware and demands money to decrypt the files, but they also exfiltrate sensitive data and threaten to release that data publicly if their demands are not met.
BlackBasta uses bcdedit to boot the device in safe mode.
Registry key HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop is created and a .jpg file is add to change the icon of encrypted files.
Once booted in safe mode, BlackBasta will iterate through the entire file system
Files (except .exe, .cmd, .bat, and .com) on the system are encrypted using ChaCha20 or RSA-4096, and their extension is changed to .basta.

The files <random-letters>.ico and <random-letters>.jpg are written to the %TEMP% directory. The .jpg file is leveraged to overwrite the desktop background and appears as follows: "Your network is encrypted by the Black Basta group. Instructions in the file readme.txt"

acts.n: Indicator Removal on Host: File Deletion
acts.d: BlackBasta attempts to delete malicious batch files.
